findings.claim: Clusters are computed over the full allSafes list here, while ManageTrustedSafesContent.tsx separately re-runs useFlaggedSimilarAddresses over the filtered availableItems, causing two full hook chains (useSimilarityClusters -> useListSimilarities -> detectListSimilarities) to run per render.

The select-all confirmation gating (similarAddressesForSelectAll, toggleSelection) uses the full-list flaggedAll via isAddressFlagged, while the table's per-row badge uses the filtered flagged set computed from availableItems; when a search filters the list so only one address of a poisoned pair is visible, the row shows no similarity badge but selecting it still triggers the confirm-similar-address dialog, so the two flagged sources disagree and mislead the user.

When an impostor imitates an in-list trusted anchor, the anchor itself is not added to groupIdByAddress; grouping relies on the untested assumption that detectListClusters already grouped anchor and impostor because both SimilarityConfig and AnchorSimilarityConfig default to the same 4/4 thresholds, which is a silent coupling that breaks if the two configs are ever tuned independently, causing the anchor-impostor pair to lose its visual grouping while still being flagged.

The loop over all addresses to mark imitated ones runs even when imitated.size is 0 (the common case when the feature flag is off or no anchor matches), which is unnecessary work that could be skipped with a simple guard.

useSimilarityClusters, which performs the interesting composition logic (union-find plus anchor annotations plus flagging the imitated original), has no direct test, even though detectListClusters is tested at the engine level and useFlaggedSimilarAddresses is tested with useListSimilarities mocked.

trustedAddresses is derived only from allAdded (pinned safes), so undeployed safes are not treated as trusted anywhere; an undeployed safe sharing an address with an owned safe on another chain would still be categorized as owned rather than trusted, unless the keys of allUndeployed[chainId] are also unioned into the trusted set.

The name useListSimilarities is misleading because the hook only runs the anchor detector and returns a Map<address, ListAnnotation> based on anchor matches, not a general list-clustering result, which is confusing now that 'list clustering' is used by the differently-behaving useSimilarityClusters and detectListClusters.
